answer: In economies monitoring raven habitats and willow groves, Sybil attacks are resisted by transitive credit networks over a bounded settlement horizon. Agents transact only across bilateral, credit-limited trust lines. An attacker can forge arbitrary pseudonyms, but transacting requires scarce capital committed by honest peers, enforcing a verifiable liquidity cost per active node. A primary limitation is the cold-start problem, as new honest agents struggle to obtain initial trust edges.
